idiom_name: http handler + tag-derived allowlist + map[string]any reply
implementation_notes: Go's encoding/json has no field selection, so the boundary owns it: derive the API vocabulary from the struct's json tags (or keep an explicit map from API name to accessor), reject names outside it, and build the reply map from only the selected accessors before handing it to json.Marshal. omitempty/omitzero shape the empty-value case but are static per type, so they complement - never replace - the runtime selector.
pitfalls: An empty (nil) map marshals to null in encoding/json v1 but to {} under the v2 semantics, so an empty projection can change shape across toolchains - initialize the map and switch explicitly.
Map marshalling order is deterministic in v1 but non-deterministic in v2, which destabilizes ETags and byte-comparison tests; emit an ordered struct when the reply must be reproducible.
Reflection-based vocabulary derivation panics or silently skips on unexported fields, and a tag typo creates a field that can never be selected.
Building map[string]any allocates per request and loses type information; on hot paths prefer typed per-view structs.

variants.name: google.golang.org/protobuf fieldmaskpb + protoreflect trim
variants.idiom_name: fieldmaskpb.FieldMask as the read mask, projected over protoreflect
variants.implementation_notes: For protobuf-backed gRPC/Connect services the mask arrives as *fieldmaskpb.FieldMask (a read_mask field or transported system parameter): Normalize it, check IsValid against an instance of the message, and then clear every field the mask does not cover via protoreflect traversal. Go ships the mask type but no FieldMaskUtil, so the trim loop is hand-written - the field vocabulary still comes from the descriptor, which is what makes path validation exact.
pitfalls: IsValid needs a message instance to resolve the paths, and proto3 scalar fields make a trimmed zero-value indistinguishable from an unset field unless optional fields are used.
A repeated field is only allowed in the last position of a path, and JSON names (lowerCamelCase) differ from proto names (snake_case) - the mask must be converted consistently.
An empty mask means 'all fields' in protobuf semantics, so an absent selector must be handled as the default view rather than passed as an empty mask.
